summary: Two complementary automated pipelines for detecting two-level system (TLS) defects in superconducting transmons via SWAP spectroscopy are presented: one-dimensional decay-rate fitting (1D-DRF) and a deterministic computer-vision framework (2D-CV) exploiting temporal persistence of coherent population suppression. Deployed across 52 flux-tunable transmons on Rigetti processors, both methods reveal that moderate ($\sim 10\%$) post-fabrication frequency trimming via Alternating-Bias Assisted Annealing (ABAA) selectively suppresses strongly dissipative defect channels while leaving total TLS count unchanged, reducing span-integrated loss by a factor of $\sim 2$ ($6.9\,\text{kHz} \to 3.1\,\text{kHz}$).
motivation: TLS defects in dielectric interfaces and Josephson junction barriers remain a primary decoherence mechanism in superconducting transmon qubits, necessitating scalable, automated characterization across multi-qubit processors to enable hardware diagnostics and defect engineering.
method: Two independent analysis pipelines extract TLS statistics from time-resolved SWAP spectroscopy: 1D-DRF identifies defects via localized $\Gamma_1$ enhancements using rolling median filtering and significance thresholding; 2D-CV applies anisotropic Gaussian scale-space filtering ($\sigma_t = 80$, $\sigma_f = 10$ pixels) to native 2D population maps and exploits temporal persistence projection ($\rho(f) > 0.14$) to decouple resonant loss from baseline drift, both quantified via Lorentzian fits ($\mathcal{I}_{\text{TLS}} = \pi A \gamma_f$) to extract frequency-integrated loss strength $\propto v_\perp^2$.
result: Consensus detections ($n = 597$ pairs, $\delta f = 25\,\text{MHz}$) show near-unity correlation ($r = 0.88$) in physical loss strengths across six orders of magnitude; mean TLS count unchanged under ABAA ($38.7 \pm 17.7$ vs. $37.9 \pm 11.3$ defects/qubit, $p > 0.8$), but high-dissipation tail ($\mathcal{I}_{\text{TLS}} > 10^{11}\,\text{Hz}^2$) systematically depleted, demonstrating selective suppression of strongest-coupled channels without defect elimination.
